catalogue_metadata.scope_notes: Extraction of non-agentic structural, domain, and infrastructural architecture patterns in the cas_runner system.
analysis_limits: Repository source inspection based on available symbols and directory structures
Focus restricted strictly to non-agentic structural layers (Pydantic models, CLI/Runner pipelines, governance engines, filesystem repositories)

system_map.overview: cas_runner is structured as a modular Python package layered across Presentation (CLI, Bootstrap), Application (FlowRunner, GovernanceActionService), Domain (Governance Models, Steering Entities, Health Models), and Infrastructure/IO (Filesystem Knowledge Store, LiteLLM / Mock Client Adapters).

layers.name: Presentation & CLI
layers.purpose: Entry points for CLI execution, bootstrap orchestration, and workspace initialization

layers.name: Application & Orchestration
layers.purpose: Execution flow coordination, compliance checking, and governance action dispatching

layers.name: Domain Models & Logic
layers.purpose: Domain typing, health status evaluation, architectural deltas, and state transition registries

layers.name: Infrastructure & Adapters
layers.purpose: External AI provider adapters, mock clients, and filesystem-backed knowledge structures

components.name: GovernanceActionEngine
components.responsibility: Executes state transitions and registers valid state machine transitions for governance entities.

components.name: FlowRunner
components.responsibility: Coordinates execution flows and sequences steps across workspace data and governance rules.

components.name: ComplianceEngine
components.responsibility: Evaluates architectural and policy compliance findings against defined governance models.

components.name: HealthModelEvaluator
components.responsibility: Computes health statuses and diagnostic reasons from governance inventory metrics.

patterns.name: Pydantic Domain Entity Modeling
patterns.summary: Formalizes domain concepts as strongly typed, immutable or validated Pydantic data schemas across governance and steering domains.
patterns.intent: Ensure strict type safety, input validation, and clear serialization contracts across runtime boundaries.
patterns.context: Governance, compliance, and steering pipelines parse heterogeneous JSON/YAML files and need consistent in-memory representation.
forces: High variance in filesystem inputs requires rigorous validation before execution
Serialization/deserialization between disk representations and runtime engines must be transparent and robust
patterns.solution: Define data contracts as Pydantic models encapsulating fields, enumerations, and validation logic without coupling to I/O routines.
implementation_signals: Inheritance from BaseModel or Pydantic dataclasses
Use of Enums (e.g. GitChangeType, HealthStatus) for finite states
Hierarchical entity compositions like GovernanceInventory and CapabilitySet

evidence.note: Provides formal structural typing for governance state, health, metrics, and compliance items.
Models repository changes, architectural capabilities, and deltas as typed schemas.

benefits: Eliminates silent data corruption by rejecting invalid payloads at system boundaries
Provides immediate schema documentation and IDE autocompletion
costs: Runtime validation overhead on large document collections
Rigid models can require migration layers if storage formats evolve
failure_modes: Schema deserialization exceptions when incoming legacy JSON does not match newer schema versions

patterns.reuse_notes: Directly reusable for any data pipeline demanding deterministic serialization contracts.

patterns.name: Transition Registry State Machine
patterns.summary: Decouples lifecycle state validations and transitions from execution logic using an explicit registration map.
patterns.intent: Centralize valid entity state transitions and their corresponding action handlers to prevent illegal lifecycle moves.
patterns.context: Governance artifacts (proposals, rules, decisions) transition through distinct lifecycle phases that must trigger specific actions.
forces: Scattering conditional if/else blocks for lifecycle state checks leads to fragile transitions
New transitions must be registerable without modifying consumer execution paths
patterns.solution: Encapsulate allowed transition matrices inside a dedicated TransitionRegistry, queried by the GovernanceActionEngine before dispatching actions.
implementation_signals: Explicit registry class mapping (current_state, target_state) -> handler/validator
Separation of registry configuration from the execution engine

evidence.note: Maintains transition rules and drives deterministic action execution.

benefits: Strict validation of valid state paths prevents data corruption
Pluggable transition registrations make extending the lifecycle model straightforward
costs: Adds indirection compared to simple imperative function transitions
failure_modes: Unregistered transitions can halt operations if fallback policies are not defined

patterns.reuse_notes: Applicable across entity lifecycle engines, document workflow systems, and approval gates.

patterns.name: Service Facade Orchestration
patterns.summary: Aggregates fine-grained domain engines (compliance, action, transitions) into a cohesive service facade for consumers.
patterns.intent: Provide a simplified, consolidated interface to complex sub-systems such as compliance engines and action registries.
patterns.context: Clients (CLI, background workflows) require single operation endpoints to process governance lifecycle events without manually orchestrating engines.
forces: Consumers should not need to instantiate and chain ComplianceEngine and GovernanceActionEngine directly
Transactions and operational boundaries must be coordinated centrally
patterns.solution: Expose a high-level GovernanceActionService that coordinates calls between the ComplianceEngine and GovernanceActionEngine.
implementation_signals: Service class composing multiple lower-level engines
High-level transactional or multi-step execution methods

evidence.note: Acts as the application entry point coordinating compliance and action engines.

benefits: Decouples CLI/runner presentation layers from low-level validation and transition mechanics
Ensures consistent sequencing of compliance verification before action execution
costs: Can become a fat service if cross-cutting concerns are not delegated
failure_modes: Partial execution failures across composed engines if transactional rollbacks are missing

patterns.reuse_notes: Standard application service pattern for domain-driven Python architectures.

patterns.name: Client Adapter and Test Double
patterns.summary: Separates real external network/API communication from test environments via symmetric client interfaces.
patterns.intent: Allow offline execution, deterministic testing, and CI validation without calling live external provider APIs.
patterns.context: External integrations (such as LiteLLM API providers) are costly, non-deterministic, or unavailable during local builds and unit tests.
forces: Components requiring provider interaction must execute without active internet connections or credentials
Mock implementations must adhere to the identical call interface as real clients
patterns.solution: Implement parallel client adapters (e.g. LiteLLMClient and MockLLMClient) sharing method signatures for transparent substitution.
implementation_signals: Symmetric public methods across client implementations
Configuration-driven injection of mock clients in test suites

evidence.note: Production adapter calling external LiteLLM APIs.
Offline test double providing stubbed or simulated responses.

benefits: Fast, cost-free, deterministic testing in CI/CD environments
Isolates the rest of the application from external SDK API changes
costs: Risk of behavior drift between mock client stubs and production API edge cases
failure_modes: Mock client fails to replicate rate limits, timeout exceptions, or specific serialization errors

patterns.reuse_notes: Fundamental pattern for third-party SDK and external cloud service integration.

patterns.name: File-System Structured Knowledge Repository
patterns.summary: Employs an organized directory hierarchy of markdown, YAML, and JSON files as the persistent source of truth.
patterns.intent: Persist architecture decisions, rules, patterns, and runtimes directly in version-controlled directory structures.
patterns.context: Architecture knowledge must be transparent, reviewable via Git Pull Requests, and easily inspectable by human architects and scripts.
forces: Databases add operational complexity and obscure Git-centric change tracking
Hierarchical knowledge requires clear categorization (global, project-specific, runtime, templates)
patterns.solution: Partition knowledge into standardized filesystem buckets: global/ (cross-cutting decisions and models), projects/ (sub-system workspaces), runtime/ (ephemeral traces and evaluation profiles), and templates/.
implementation_signals: Structured filesystem tree with explicit classification folders (decisions, rules, signals)
Templates defining standard document structures for architecture artifacts
Workspace bootstrap scripts synchronizing repository scaffolds

evidence.note: Directory structure containing global, projects, runtime, and templates sub-trees.
Provisions workspace directories and synchronizes governance files into target projects.

benefits: Zero-dependency persistence versionable with standard Git workflows
Human-readable and editable markdown and YAML documents
costs: Lacks transactional ACID guarantees across multi-file mutations
File system scanning latency increases linearly with repository size
failure_modes: Concurrent file writes causing race conditions or corrupted YAML/JSON structures

patterns.reuse_notes: Ideal for GitOps-driven architecture management tools, static site generators, and developer portals.

patterns.name: Declarative Health Scoring Pipeline
patterns.summary: Pure functional evaluation pipeline deriving health status and diagnostic reasoning from state metrics.
patterns.intent: Compute deterministic health states and diagnostic explanations from input metrics without side effects.
patterns.context: Dashboards and CLI tools require consistent, explainable health diagnostics based on governance metrics.
forces: Health computation rules should be isolated from presentation and persistence code
Health status must provide actionable, human-readable explanations alongside raw enum states
patterns.solution: Provide isolated functions (calculate_health, get_health_reasons) operating on immutable state objects to return HealthStatus and diagnostic lists.
implementation_signals: Pure Python functions accepting metric objects and returning status/reasons
Separation of calculation logic from dashboard rendering

evidence.note: Functional evaluation of health states and human-readable diagnostic reasons.

benefits: Easily unit-tested without mocking I/O or state
Predictable and reproducible evaluation across both CLI and web portal components
costs: Threshold changes require code deployments unless externalized into configuration
failure_modes: Missing edge case handling in metric values causing uncaught evaluation exceptions

patterns.reuse_notes: Applicable for status monitors, health-check probes, and operational dashboards.

anti_patterns.name: Monolithic Runner Flow Coupling
symptoms: FlowRunner handles step orchestration, I/O dispatch, and rule evaluation directly within single execution methods
Difficulty unit testing individual workflow stages without executing full runner cycles
impact: High maintenance cost as new pipeline steps are added
Increased risk of regressions when modifying flow execution order
suggested_remediation: Refactor FlowRunner into a pipeline or command pattern where each step implements an independent Step interface
Inject dependencies (parsers, evaluators, notifiers) into individual step instances rather than the runner

anti_patterns.name: Unvalidated Filesystem Layout Assumption
symptoms: Direct reliance on relative directory paths (cas-knowledge/global, cas-knowledge/runtime) without abstracted storage provider interfaces
Failure when run from unexpected working directories
impact: Breaks portability across environments where knowledge files are mounted or stored in non-standard paths
suggested_remediation: Introduce an explicit WorkspaceProvider or StorageAdapter interface to abstract direct filesystem access
Enforce strict path resolution via configuration parameters rather than hardcoded directory structures

cross_cutting_concerns.name: Observability & Telemetry
cross_cutting_concerns.description: Integration of OpenTelemetry SDK (opentelemetry-api, opentelemetry-sdk) in dependencies for distributed tracing and operational telemetry across governance runs.

cross_cutting_concerns.name: Schema-Driven Documentation
cross_cutting_concerns.description: Generation of documentation and diagrams via mkdocs, mkdocs-material, and mkdocs-drawio reflecting the filesystem knowledge store.

open_questions.question: How are concurrent read-write collisions handled in the cas-knowledge filesystem when multiple runner instances operate on the same repository?
open_questions.context: No file locking or transaction journaling mechanisms are evident in the bootstrap and runner modules.
